title: New Troubadours — events_normalized.json
description: Reference schema for the site's combined events data file. Field presence varies a lot in practice (most fields are optional / left as empty strings rather than omitted), so this schema is documentation-oriented: it is permissive (additionalProperties: true throughout) rather than strict, and exists to record the shapes actually in use rather than to validate/reject real data.

story_walk_details.description: RESERVED, currently unused/empty. Enrichment-only data for repertoireShow records with isStoryWalk: true — keyed by the SAME id as the corresponding entry in repertoire_shows (not a separate id space), e.g. story_walk_details["sally-port-history-portsmouth-pubs"]. Intended for fields that don't fit repertoireShow's shape at all: a geojson route, an ordered list of waypoints (each with its own name/description/maybe a photo), total walk duration, food/drink availability along the route. Purely additive — nothing currently reads this object, so it can be introduced at any time without touching display code. Only relevant to a record that already exists in repertoire_shows; there is no reason to have an entry here without a matching repertoire_shows entry.

dateOrDates.description: A single DD/MM/YYYY date string, OR an array of such strings for a multi-night run at the same venue (e.g. several consecutive nights of one tour stop). Code that reads `.date` should always normalize via Array.isArray() before use — see expandTourDates()/forEachDateInRange() in shared_utils.js.

type.description: Which moment this time refers to. null means a plain, unlabelled time — used when there's just one time and no need to label it.

time.description: The time itself, in whatever casual format the site already uses (e.g. '7.30pm', '8pm', '7:30-9pm').

structuredTimeList.description: Optional structured alternative/companion to the free-text `time` field on the same record. When present, the event builder auto-generates `time` by textualising these entries — e.g. a single unlabelled entry becomes '8pm'; labelled entries join as 'Doors 7pm, Start 8.30pm'. `time` remains the field everything else reads; `structured_time` is only ever a convenience for producing/editing it, and `time` can still be hand-edited afterwards without touching this.

type.description: What kind of price this entry represents. Free text, not a strict enum, so new categories can be added without a schema change — but the event builder's UI and renderer specifically understand: 'standard' (or omitted), 'concession', 'advance', 'earlybird', 'door', 'online', 'member', 'donation', 'pwyw' (pay what you can/want), 'free', and 'tier' (a named tier/band, e.g. a festival's Tier 1/Tier 2 — pair with `label`). Anything else is still rendered, just using `label` verbatim rather than a built-in wording.

label.description: Display label. Required in practice for type 'tier' or any custom type (e.g. 'Tier 1', 'Benefactor', 'NUS members') since the renderer has no built-in wording for those; optional elsewhere as a wording override (e.g. 'suggested minimum' instead of the default 'suggested' on a pwyw/donation entry).

amount.description: The headline amount for this entry, in pounds (e.g. 10, 1.5). Omitted for a plain 'free' entry with no note; for 'pwyw'/'donation' this is treated as a suggested/minimum amount rather than a fixed price.

fee.description: An additional fee layered on top of `amount` for this entry specifically (e.g. a booking fee), rendered as '(+ £Y)' — this is exactly the '£10 (+ £1.50)' pattern common in this site's existing price text, and is also already specifically recognised and stripped out by parseEventPrice() in stats.js when it derives a face value for stats, so text generated in this shape stays compatible with that.

structuredPriceList.description: Optional structured alternative/companion to the free-text `price` field on the same record — mirrors how `structured_time` relates to `time`. When present, the event builder auto-generates `price` by rendering and joining these entries with ' / ' (e.g. a single {amount:10} becomes '£10'; {amount:10, fee:1.5} becomes '£10 (+ £1.50)'; {type:'advance', amount:8} plus {type:'door', amount:10} becomes '£8 advance / £10 door'). `price` remains the field everything else reads (including parseEventPrice() in stats.js, which only ever looks at the text); `structured_price` is only ever a convenience for producing/editing it, stays fully hand-editable afterwards, and is intentionally kept simple for now — deliberately not attempting to model every real-world pricing scheme (e.g. multi-day festival passes with deposits) as structured data, just the common shapes (standard/concession/advance/door/tiers/donation/pwyw/free, each with an optional fee).

eventId.description: Optional stable, explicit identifier for a specificEvent/musicEvent/poetryEvent record, used as its event.html permalink (?event=) whenever set — see resolveEventId() in shared_utils.js. When a record has no eventId, resolveEventId() generates one instead, in the form `yyyymmdd-performerId-venueId` (the event's own date + its performer_id, or the first entry of performer_ids if there's no single performer_id, + its venue_id) via buildStructuredEventId() — replacing the older `${name}-${date.getTime()}` scheme buildEventId() produced (that function is kept, marked @deprecated, only because other pages/older permalinks out in the wild may still rely on its exact output; new code should prefer resolveEventId()). The generated yyyymmdd-performerId-venueId form isn't guaranteed unique — e.g. the same performer doing two different shows at the same venue on the same day would generate the same id for both — and nothing generates or resolves eventId automatically checks for that. Where a collision is possible or has happened, set eventId here by hand to a value that disambiguates the records; the event builder's Enrich tab includes a checker that suggests a generated id for any record missing one and flags likely collisions among its own suggestions, but leaves it to the maintainer to actually resolve them.

youtubeUrl.description: Optional YouTube trailer URL (watch/youtu.be/shorts/embed form). Rendered via getYouTubeEmbedUrl() in shared_utils.js, which validates the host and converts it to a safe youtube-nocookie.com /embed/ URL; anything else is silently ignored by the front end.

eventFlyersList.description: Preferred way to give a single date/event MORE THAN ONE flyer (e.g. a reprint, or separate artwork supplied by different promoters). Coexists with that record's own `event_flyer` (and, for specificEvents only, the now-removed legacy `event_flyer2`) — all are merged, in order, by getEventLevelFlyers() in shared_utils.js, de-duplicated by filename. Each entry is either a plain filename string, or an object with an optional caption. Same shape as tour.touring_event_flyers, just at the individual date/event level rather than the whole-tour level.

oneOf.description: Just a filename — gets an auto-generated label ("Event flyer", or "Event flyer 1", "Event flyer 2"... if there's more than one across all fields).

label.description: Optional caption shown under the thumbnail. Aliases: caption, title.

venue.description: A venue record, keyed by a slug id (e.g. "wardrobe-theatre-bristol") in the top-level `venues` object.

id.description: Same as the object's own key; kept inline for convenience.

venue_type.description: Venue type category, resolved against the VENUE_TYPES dict in shared_guessers.js: a slug (e.g. "pub-bar-cafe", "live-music-venue"), the full label text of one (legacy data — every venue set before that dict existed stores the label directly, e.g. "Pub / bar / café", and resolveVenueType() in shared_guessers.js still matches those, so nothing needs to be migrated), or free text that matches neither. An unmatched value is displayed verbatim rather than collapsed into "Other / unknown", so nothing typed by hand is silently discarded. Current VENUE_TYPES slugs: pub-bar-cafe, village-hall, arts-centre, theatre, church, museum-historic, barn-rural-outdoor, online, bookshop, social-club, live-music-venue, other. A single value OR an array of values for a venue that's genuinely more than one thing, e.g. ["pub-bar-cafe", "live-music-venue"] — code reading this should normalize via Array.isArray(), same as dateOrDates/podcastUrls; see resolveVenueTypesForVenue() in shared_guessers.js, which always returns an array (of resolved {slug, label, colour} entries) and is what venues.js/stats.js call rather than reading this field raw. The event builder's Venue form offers the known labels via a datalist and can auto-suggest one from the venue name using classifyVenueType() in shared_guessers.js (the same heuristic the Stats page falls back to), but any string, or comma-separated list of strings, is valid, including ones outside VENUE_TYPES, and the field can be left unset. If unset, venue_type is effectively re-derived on the fly by that same heuristic wherever it's needed — setting it explicitly here just lets a person override or confirm that guess, and (as of this revision) that override is actually honoured by venues.js/stats.js rather than silently ignored.

ticketing_url.description: Variant spelling of `tickets_url` (one venue uses it). Kept for data as it stands; `tickets_url` is the standard name here.

performer.description: A performer/artist record, keyed by a slug id (e.g. "daniel-morden") in the top-level `performers` object. Can also represent a troupe/duo via `troupe` + `performer_ids`.

id.description: Same as the object's own key.

musician.description: Identifies this performer as a musician.

isBand.description: Identifies this performer as a band.

poet.description: Marks this performer as a punk-poet/spoken-word artist — shown as a badge on their profile page and used to classify their appearances for the performance-type filters (performers/venues listings).

troupe.description: True if this record represents a group/duo rather than an individual.

performer_ids.description: Member performer ids, when `troupe` is true.

members.description: Display names of troupe members (alternative/companion to performer_ids).

podcast_appearances.description: One-off guest spots on other people's podcasts (as opposed to performer.podcast, which is a podcast the performer runs themself). Rendered as a collapsible list on the performer profile page; each entry's audio is only fetched if/when the visitor opens that entry's player.

youtube_videos.description: YouTube videos of this performer (e.g. recorded storytelling/performances), shown as a collapsible list of nested collapsibles on the performer profile page. Each video's embed is only created if/when the visitor opens that specific video's collapsible, and is torn down again if they close it.

ticketing_url.description: Performer's own ticket shop/organiser page (e.g. TicketSource, Eventbrite). Variant spelling of `tickets_url` — both are in use.

youtube.description: Link to the performer's YouTube channel (as opposed to `youtube_videos`, which lists individual videos).

podcastX.description: [TO DO — looks like a stray/disabled copy of `podcast`: one record (owen-staton) has a podbean URL under this name, so it is not read as a podcast link. Confirm whether it should be renamed to `podcast`.]

youtubeVideo.description: One YouTube video associated with a performer.

story_name.description: Title/label shown for this video (often the story or piece performed, not necessarily the video's own YouTube title).

yt_url.description: The video's YouTube URL, in any common form (watch?v=, youtu.be/, /embed/, /shorts/).

podcastUrls.description: One or more podcast links for a performer (episode pages, show pages, or listen-on-X links — whatever the performer links to). A single URL string, OR an array of URL strings for a performer with several podcasts/series. Code that reads performer.podcast should always normalize via Array.isArray() before use — see normalisePodcastUrls() in performers.html, which renders these in the collapsible podcast section on the performer profile page.

podcastAppearance.description: One guest appearance by a performer on someone else's podcast episode. Now primarily intended for a one-off guest spot on a podcast that isn't (and may not be worth) registering in the top-level `podcasts` list — identified inline via `podcast` (and optionally `podcast_url`). Once a podcast has a podcast_id, prefer adding the appearance as an entry in that podcast's items[] (with performer_id set) instead of duplicating it here; `podcast_id` is still accepted for backward compatibility but shouldn't be used for new entries. `audio_url` should point directly at the episode's playable media file.

podcast_id.description: References podcasts[].podcast_id. Deprecated in favour of an entry in that podcast's items[] — kept only for backward compatibility with existing data.

podcast.description: Podcast/series name, given directly when there's no podcast_id (or as a fallback label if the id can't be resolved).

podcast_url.description: The podcast's own homepage, used alongside an inline `podcast` name.

episode_name.description: Episode title, or a short description of the appearance.

audio_url.description: Direct link to the playable episode audio (e.g. an .mp3), not a feed or webpage.

tourDate.description: One stop on a tour, inside tour.tour_dates[].

fb_event.description: Facebook event id, used to build a facebook.com/events/{id} link.

event_flyer.description: Filename for a flyer specific to this individual date.

tour_flyer.description: Per-date override of the tour's headline flyer (rare — usually set at tour level instead).

video_trailer.description: Per-date override of the tour's video_trailer; falls back to the tour-level value if omitted.

club_event.description: Opts this date into a club's own event listing — set to the matching club id from `events[].club`. Picked up by the story-club page alongside that club's regular nights.

isFestival.description: Marks this tour date as actually a festival appearance.

age_rating.description: Optional free-text age-suitability descriptor for display, e.g. 'Family friendly', 'Suitable for ages 8+', 'Adult content (18+)'. Not a strict enum. The event builder's Enrich tab and the event form's "Suggest from description" action can both propose one by parsing common cues out of `description` (via parseAgeRatingFromText() in shared_guessers.js) — always a suggestion to review, not authoritative.

min_age.description: Optional minimum recommended age as a plain number (e.g. 8, 12, 18), kept separate from age_rating so there's something reliably sortable/filterable for stats even though age_rating itself is free text. Left null/unset when no specific minimum is implied (e.g. 'Family friendly' doesn't imply one).

event_warning.description: Optional general-purpose content note, e.g. 'Contains strong language', 'Discusses bereavement', 'Strobe lighting used'. Distinct from age_rating/min_age, which are about audience suitability rather than describing content — kept deliberately general (not a strict enum) rather than a narrower 'content_warning' name, so it can also cover non-content-related heads-up notes (e.g. accessibility/venue caveats) without renaming later.

city.description: Rare free-text city override (normally derived from venue_id instead).

venue.description: Rare free-text venue-name override (normally derived from venue_id instead).

performer_id.description: Rare per-date performer override, e.g. a guest replacing the usual performer for one stop.

description_prefix.description:
Rare per-date text prepended ahead of the resolved show/tour description when this date's listing is displayed — e.g. a promoter's own billing copy ("The Crick Crack Club presents..."). Rendered as `{description_prefix}



{description}` (see combineDescriptionWithPrefix() in shared_utils.js), i.e. as its own leading paragraph, not merged into the description text itself.

date_added.description: DD/MM/YYYY — when this date was added, used to surface it in the "new events" panel. Same meaning as showDate.date_added and the event records' date_added (the event builder writes this on tour dates).

related_event.description: Free-text name of a wider event this date is part of (e.g. 'Cornwall Tattoo Convention'). Display/reference only — unlike wider_event on specificEvents it is not a key into `festivals`.

tour.description: A tour record, keyed by a slug id (e.g. "debs-newbold-dauntless-2026") in the top-level `tours` object. Rendered on the tour-guide page and merged into the events calendar, one calendar entry per tour_dates entry.

repertoire_id.description: Key into the top-level `repertoire_shows` object, when this tour is a touring run of an already-registered repertoire show. When set, applyRepertoireInheritance() in shared_utils.js copies name, showname, performer_id, performer_ids, video_trailer and touring_event_flyer from that repertoire_shows entry onto this tour for any of those fields the tour doesn't set itself (each is overridden individually — a tour can set its own name but still inherit performer_id, for instance). tour_description is a special case: it falls back to the repertoire show's `description` specifically, rather than being listed as a plain inheritable field, since the two field names differ. This runs once when events_normalized.json is loaded, so every consumer (tour page, calendar, search, flyers) sees the already-resolved values without needing repertoire-aware logic of its own.

name.description: Short show name without the run/performer suffix. Inherited from repertoire_shows[repertoire_id].name if omitted — see repertoire_id.

tour_description.description:
Long-form description; paragraphs are conventionally separated by a blank double-line (



) in the source text. If omitted and repertoire_id is set, falls back to repertoire_shows[repertoire_id].description — see repertoire_id.

touring_event_flyer.description: Headline flyer image filename representing the WHOLE tour (shown once on the flyers page, rather than repeated per date). Also accepted under the legacy alias `tour_flyer`.

tour_flyer.description: Legacy alias for touring_event_flyer — either name is accepted.

touring_event_flyers.description: Preferred way to give a tour MORE THAN ONE headline flyer (e.g. separate artwork for different legs, or a redesigned poster partway through the run). Supersedes touring_event_flyer/tour_flyer when present — all three may coexist and are merged, in order, by getTourLevelFlyers() in shared_utils.js, de-duplicated by filename. Each entry is either a plain filename string, or an object with an optional caption.

oneOf.description: Just a filename — gets an auto-generated label ("Tour flyer", or "Tour flyer 1", "Tour flyer 2"... if there's more than one across all three fields).

label.description: Optional caption shown under the thumbnail. Aliases: caption, title.

isPoetry.description: Marks this as a punk-poetry/spoken-word tour, styled with its own colour band on the events calendar.

video_trailer.description: Tour-level YouTube trailer, shown on the tour page and in the flyers page's Video Trailers section. Individual tour_dates entries may override this per-date.

price.description: Rare tour-level default price, used when a tour_date omits its own price.

tour_flyers.description: [TO DO — one tour (katy-cawkwell-lilith-autumn-winter-2026-2027) uses this plural name, which is not one of the recognised flyer fields (touring_event_flyer / tour_flyer / touring_event_flyers). Probably meant to be `touring_event_flyers`, which getTourLevelFlyers() actually merges — worth renaming in the data.]

showDate.description: One date for a repertoire show, inside show.show_dates[].

repertoire_id.description: [TO DO — flagged during schema review: no show_dates entry in the actual data sets this; the one real repertoire_id in repertoire_shows data is instead set on the repertoireShow record itself (debs-newbold-dauntless), which isn't documented anywhere in this schema either. Worth confirming whether that's a stray self-reference left over from copying the tour-level repertoire_id pattern, or genuinely meant to live at one/both of these levels, then updating data + schema to match.] Unique identifier for repertoire show.

club.description: Key into `events[].club` for the club night this date belongs to.

event_flyer.description: Flyer specific to this individual date.

video_trailer.description: Per-date override of the show's video_trailer.

date_added.description: DD/MM/YYYY — when this date was added, used to surface it in the "new events" panel.

description_prefix.description:
Rare per-date text prepended ahead of the show's description when this date's listing is displayed — e.g. a promoter's own billing copy ("The Crick Crack Club presents..."). Rendered as `{description_prefix}



{description}` (see combineDescriptionWithPrefix() in shared_utils.js), i.e. as its own leading paragraph, not merged into the description text itself.

promoter.description: LEGACY alias of `promoter_id` (used by 10 show_dates entries). Same meaning: a key into `promoters`. New records use `promoter_id`; the event builder reads this when editing and writes it back as `promoter_id`.

performer_id.description: Rare per-date performer override, e.g. a guest replacing the usual performer for one date (same as tourDate.performer_id).

age.description: Free-text age note for this date (e.g. 'Recommended 14+'). Not the standard field — age_rating/min_age are defined on the repertoireShow record itself rather than per date; this is a per-date variant seen in the data.

repertoireShow.description: A repertoire/touring show record, keyed by a slug id in the top-level `repertoire_shows` object. Similar in spirit to a tour, but typically a single show performed at various clubs/venues over time rather than a single linear tour run.

showname.description: Short show name without the performer suffix.

description.description: Referenced by tours[].repertoire_id — a tour with no tour_description of its own falls back to this. See tour.repertoire_id.

age_rating.description: Optional free-text age-suitability descriptor for display, e.g. 'Family friendly', 'Suitable for ages 8+', 'Adult content (18+)'. Not a strict enum. The event builder's Enrich tab and the event form's "Suggest from description" action can both propose one by parsing common cues out of `description` (via parseAgeRatingFromText() in shared_guessers.js) — always a suggestion to review, not authoritative.

min_age.description: Optional minimum recommended age as a plain number (e.g. 8, 12, 18), kept separate from age_rating so there's something reliably sortable/filterable for stats even though age_rating itself is free text. Left null/unset when no specific minimum is implied (e.g. 'Family friendly' doesn't imply one).

event_warning.description: Optional general-purpose content note, e.g. 'Contains strong language', 'Discusses bereavement', 'Strobe lighting used'. Distinct from age_rating/min_age, which are about audience suitability rather than describing content — kept deliberately general (not a strict enum) rather than a narrower 'content_warning' name, so it can also cover non-content-related heads-up notes (e.g. accessibility/venue caveats) without renaming later.

touring_event_flyer.description: Headline flyer image filename for the whole show (one card, not repeated per date).

touring_event_flyers.description: Preferred way to give a repertoire show MORE THAN ONE headline flyer (e.g. separate artwork for different tour legs, or a redesigned poster partway through the run) — same idea as tour.touring_event_flyers. Schema-only for now: unlike tour.touring_event_flyers (merged by getTourLevelFlyers() in shared_utils.js), nothing currently reads this field on a repertoireShow record — display code, the builder form, and getTourLevelFlyers()/getEventLevelFlyers() would all need updating to actually merge it in alongside touring_event_flyer before this has any visible effect.

isStoryWalk.description: Marks this as a promoter/guide-led story walk rather than a conventional storytelling performance — e.g. sally-port-history-portsmouth-pubs (a walking tour of pub histories, run by a promoter rather than booked club-to-club). Still a full repertoireShow record (same show_dates/venue/promoter/price shape) — this flag only changes display: excluded from "Repertoire" listings on the tour-guide and performer pages in favour of a separate "Story Walks" section there, shown with a distinct badge (but no structural change) on venue pages, and behind an off-by-default 'Show story walks' filter on the events calendar (see EVENT_TYPE_FILTERS in event_display.js). Chosen over a standalone top-level category because a story walk's core fields (dates, venue, performer, description) are identical to any other repertoire show; only its DISPLAY grouping differs. If a future story walk needs fields that don't fit repertoireShow at all, see story_walk_details below rather than adding walk-specific fields here.

video_trailer.description: Show-level YouTube trailer; individual show_dates entries may override this per-date.

repertoire_id.description: [TO DO — flagged during schema review: this only appears once in the actual data (debs-newbold-dauntless), set to the record's own key. A repertoireShow is already looked up BY that key from tours[].repertoire_id, so a matching field on the record itself is redundant unless something else is meant to read it. Confirm whether this was meant to go here at all before adding more of these — may just be a copy/paste slip from adding the tour-level field.]

show_dates.description: The normal way to give a repertoireShow its dates — one explicit entry per performance, each with its own venue/price/time/flyer/ticket_url. RESERVED, not yet supported: `schedule` + `exceptions` (see below) as an alternative to listing dates by hand, for a show/walk that genuinely repeats on a pattern.

schedule.description: RESERVED — not yet read by any processing code. An alternative to manually maintaining show_dates, for a repertoireShow (in practice: an isStoryWalk one) that recurs on a fixed pattern rather than being individually booked date by date — e.g. a story walk run '1st Saturday' every month with the same meeting point, promoter, and price throughout. Same string/object format and same engine as recurringClubEvent.schedule — reuse RecurrenceEngine.scheduledOccurrencesInRange() (recurrence-engine.js) rather than building a second recurrence parser. Deliberately NOT modelled as a recurringClubEvent instead of a repertoireShow: recurringClubEvent has no price/ticket_url (storyclubs are free meetups, not ticketed), and its identity is club-centric (rotating guest performers via feature_slots) rather than performer-centric — both wrong for a ticketed, performer-authored show/walk. This field borrows only the recurrence MECHANISM from recurringClubEvent, not its shape. Once present, `schedule` (+ optional `exceptions`, identical DD/MM/YYYY-exact / MM/YYYY-whole-month format to recurringClubEvent.exceptions) would be read by processRepertoireShows()/searchAllUpcoming() (event_display.js), repertoireShowAsTourShape() (tour_display.js), and the venue-page listing (venues.js) to generate occurrences the same way show_dates entries are read today — expanded occurrences would all share this record's single venue/price/time (unlike show_dates' per-entry overrides), consistent with why a schedule-based show wouldn't need per-date variation in the first place. Not built because no live example needs it yet — see the isStoryWalk field above for the one story walk that exists today, which uses show_dates.

exceptions.description: RESERVED, paired with `schedule` above — not yet read by any processing code. Same format as recurringClubEvent.exceptions: DD/MM/YYYY to skip/reschedule one exact occurrence, or MM/YYYY to skip every occurrence that whole month.

specificEvent.description: A one-off story/spoken-word event (specificEvents[] array) — typically a guest appearance at an existing club night, OR a standalone show that isn't part of a tour/repertoire show.

time.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's own `time` in at load time. Set here to override the club's usual time for this one date even when inheriting.

club.description: Key into `events[].club`, if this is happening at an existing club night. By itself this only associates the record with that club (e.g. so it appears on storyclub.js's club-page listing) — it does NOT by itself default any fields. Pair with `inheritClubData: true` to also have venue_id/time/price/facebook fall back to that club record wherever this record leaves them blank — see recurringClubEvent's matching fields and `inheritClubData` below.

inheritClubData.description: When true, and `club` resolves to an existing recurringClubEvent, applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) fills in this record's venue_id/time/price/facebook from that club record for any of those left blank here. Deliberately opt-in rather than automatic whenever `club` is set: a record can reference a club purely for cross-referencing/listing purposes while staying fully self-contained, and a record that's missing venue_id by oversight shouldn't silently look complete. Omit or set false for a fully standalone record. No effect if `club` is unset or doesn't resolve to a known club (a console warning is logged in that case).

price.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's own `price` in at load time. Set here to override (e.g. a guest night with a different door price) even when inheriting.

age_rating.description: Optional free-text age-suitability descriptor for display, e.g. 'Family friendly', 'Suitable for ages 8+', 'Adult content (18+)'. Not a strict enum. The event builder's Enrich tab and the event form's "Suggest from description" action can both propose one by parsing common cues out of `description` (via parseAgeRatingFromText() in shared_guessers.js) — always a suggestion to review, not authoritative.

min_age.description: Optional minimum recommended age as a plain number (e.g. 8, 12, 18), kept separate from age_rating so there's something reliably sortable/filterable for stats even though age_rating itself is free text. Left null/unset when no specific minimum is implied (e.g. 'Family friendly' doesn't imply one).

event_warning.description: Optional general-purpose content note, e.g. 'Contains strong language', 'Discusses bereavement', 'Strobe lighting used'. Distinct from age_rating/min_age, which are about audience suitability rather than describing content — kept deliberately general (not a strict enum) rather than a narrower 'content_warning' name, so it can also cover non-content-related heads-up notes (e.g. accessibility/venue caveats) without renaming later.

facebook.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's own `facebook` in at load time.

openslots.description: Whether the event has open mic/floor slots.

wider_event.description: Key into `festivals` if this is part of a larger festival.

performer.description: Free-text performer name, used when there's no matching performer_id record.

venue_id.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent with its own venue_id — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's venue_id in at load time. Set here to override (e.g. a one-off relocation) even when inheriting.

datetimes.description: Optional explicit start/end datetime pairs, for events needing more than a date+time string (e.g. multi-day or precisely timed entries).

dates.description: Full list of dates in a series of which THIS record is one date (each record's own date is in `date`). In current data, 5 records for one series each carry the whole 5-date list here while `date` holds just that record's night. Informational — `date` is what date-driven code reads.

isStoryWalk.description: Marks a one-off story walk (3 specificEvents records do this), mirroring repertoireShow.isStoryWalk — see that field for how story walks are displayed.

event_url.description: Link to the event's own web page (as opposed to `link`, `ticket_url` or `facebook`).

musicEvent.description: A one-off music event (musicEvents[] array) — same shape as specificEvent but always implicitly isMusic.

time.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's own `time` in at load time.

club.description: Key into `events[].club`, if this is happening at an existing club night. By itself this only associates the record with that club — it does NOT by itself default any fields. Pair with `inheritClubData: true` to also have venue_id/time/price/facebook fall back to that club record wherever this record leaves them blank.

inheritClubData.description: When true, and `club` resolves to an existing recurringClubEvent, applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) fills in this record's venue_id/time/price/facebook from that club record for any of those left blank here. Deliberately opt-in rather than automatic whenever `club` is set — see specificEvent.inheritClubData for the full rationale. Omit or set false for a fully standalone record.

price.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's own `price` in at load time.

age_rating.description: Optional free-text age-suitability descriptor for display, e.g. 'Family friendly', 'Suitable for ages 8+', 'Adult content (18+)'. Not a strict enum. The event builder's Enrich tab and the event form's "Suggest from description" action can both propose one by parsing common cues out of `description` (via parseAgeRatingFromText() in shared_guessers.js) — always a suggestion to review, not authoritative.

min_age.description: Optional minimum recommended age as a plain number (e.g. 8, 12, 18), kept separate from age_rating so there's something reliably sortable/filterable for stats even though age_rating itself is free text. Left null/unset when no specific minimum is implied (e.g. 'Family friendly' doesn't imply one).

event_warning.description: Optional general-purpose content note, e.g. 'Contains strong language', 'Discusses bereavement', 'Strobe lighting used'. Distinct from age_rating/min_age, which are about audience suitability rather than describing content — kept deliberately general (not a strict enum) rather than a narrower 'content_warning' name, so it can also cover non-content-related heads-up notes (e.g. accessibility/venue caveats) without renaming later.

tour_flyer.description: Rare — used when a music event is also linked to a tour-level flyer.

facebook.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's own `facebook` in at load time. Not commonly set directly on musicEvents today, but supported the same way as specificEvent/poetryEvent since applyClubInheritance() treats all three the same.

venue_id.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent with its own venue_id — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's venue_id in at load time.

date_added.description: DD/MM/YYYY — when this event was added, used to surface it in the "new events" panel.

poetryEvent.description: A one-off spoken-word/punk-poetry event (poetryEvents[] array) — same shape as musicEvent/specificEvent but always implicitly isPoetry. facebook.description: Required unless `club` + `inheritClubData: true` resolve to an existing recurringClubEvent — in that case this can be left blank and applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies the club's own `facebook` in at load time.

recurringClubEvent.description: A recurring story-club/open-mic night (events[] array) — the home record for a `club` id referenced elsewhere via specificEvents[].club, show_dates[].club, etc.

club.description: Short slug/id used to cross-reference this club from other record types. Often (but not necessarily) the same id as a `promoters[]` entry's promoter_id, if the club is run by a promoter worth registering there.

exceptions.description: Dates the schedule should skip — DD/MM/YYYY for a single date, or MM/YYYY to skip every occurrence in that month.

time.description: Also serves as the default `time` for any specificEvent/musicEvent/poetryEvent that references this club via `club` AND sets `inheritClubData: true`, when that record leaves its own `time` blank — see applyClubInheritance() in shared_utils.js.

price.description: Also serves as the default `price` for any specificEvent/musicEvent/poetryEvent that references this club via `club` AND sets `inheritClubData: true`, when that record leaves its own `price` blank — see applyClubInheritance() in shared_utils.js.

venue_id.description: Also serves as the default `venue_id` for any specificEvent/musicEvent/poetryEvent that references this club via `club` AND sets `inheritClubData: true`, when that record leaves its own `venue_id` blank — see applyClubInheritance() in shared_utils.js.

club_flyer.description: Generic flyer shown when there's no upcoming specific-event flyer for this club.

club_flyers.description: Additional flyer artwork for this club, distinct from the single club_flyer above. A filename prefixed YYYY_MM_DD (e.g. '2026_03_15_special_guest.jpg') is treated as a one-off/legacy flyer for that specific date's occurrence rather than generic ongoing club artwork — see parseDatedClubFlyer() in shared_utils.js. Renamed from the previous generic `flyers` name for consistency with club_flyer and the rest of the site's _flyer/_flyers naming convention; flyers.js, storyclub.js, venues.js, and event_display.js all read this field by name.

feature_slots.description: Rotating guest-performer bookings for specific future occurrences of this club night, keyed by date rather than stored as separate records. Each entry is a 2-element [date, performer_id] tuple: date is a DD/MM/YYYY string matched against the occurrence being rendered, performer_id is a key into the top-level `performers` object. Read by featuredGuestForDate() in storyclub.js and the feature-slot matching in processRecurringEvents()/the equivalent block further down event_display.js, both of which do `slots.find(s => s[0] === dateStr)` and then look up `s[1]` in the performers table.

prefixItems.description: DD/MM/YYYY date of the occurrence this feature slot applies to.
Key into the top-level `performers` object for the featured guest on that date.

facebook.description: Also serves as the default `facebook` for any specificEvent/musicEvent/poetryEvent that references this club via `club` AND sets `inheritClubData: true`, when that record leaves its own `facebook` blank — see applyClubInheritance() in shared_utils.js.

tickets_url.description: Note the plural name — distinct from specificEvent/musicEvent/poetryEvent's singular `ticket_url`. Deliberately NOT one of the fields applyClubInheritance() (shared_utils.js) copies onto events at this club: a guest night's booking page/capacity is often different from the club's own, so it's left for each event to set explicitly rather than defaulted.

flyers.description: LEGACY name for `club_flyers`, still used by 4 clubs (storytellingsunday, ease, plymouth-story-circle, quirkytales) — each with a single YYYY_MM_DD-prefixed one-off flyer. club_flyers is the name this schema says flyers.js/storyclub.js/venues.js/event_display.js read; if that's so, these 4 flyers are currently not being picked up and the field should be renamed in the data.

ticketing_url.description: The club's ticket shop/organiser page (one club, forgingfantastical, uses this name rather than `tickets_url`).

themes.description: Per-occurrence themes: a list of [date, theme] pairs, same tuple shape as feature_slots (date first). One club (southdevonstorytellers) has this. NOTE the dates there are not all valid DD/MM/YYYY ('28/20/2026', '23rd/12/2026') — worth fixing in the data.

online.description: True for a club that meets online (one club, southamptonSC). Note: showDate.online is a string attendance mode ("online"/"hybrid"/"in-person"), whereas on a club record it is a plain boolean.

promoter.description: An entry in the top-level `promoters` registry — a promoter/production company in its own right. A promoter_id is frequently (but not necessarily) the same id already used as a bare `club` slug elsewhere (events[].club, specificEvents[].club, etc.) — this registry exists to give that id a name, link, and associated venues/artists once it's worth doing so, without requiring anything already referencing the slug to change. Events reference a promoter via `promoter_id` (specificEvents/musicEvents/poetryEvents, tour_dates, show_dates, clubs); The event builder's New Promoter tab creates and edits these entries.

promoter_id.description: Stable id for this promoter, often reused as a `club` value elsewhere.

promoter_venues.description: Keys into the top-level `venues` object — venues this promoter regularly puts events on at.

promoter_artists.description: Keys into the top-level `performers` object — performers this promoter regularly books, as a general roster rather than tied to any specific event.

description.description:
About this promoter, About this promoter. Paragraphs separated by a blank double-line (



), same convention as tour_description.

ticketing_url.description: The promoter's own ticket shop/organiser page (e.g. a TicketSource or Eventbrite organiser page). Note the name: `ticketing_url`, not `tickets_url`/`ticket_url` as on other record types — this is what the data actually uses (5 promoters, plus clubs/venues/performers).

url.description: Alternative to `promoter_link` for the promoter's website — one registry entry (woolly-tellers) uses this instead. The event builder's New Promoter tab folds `url` into `promoter_link` when it saves an edited record; new entries should use `promoter_link`.

schedule.description: Per-day/per-stage running order. Shape varies by festival — treated as opaque/free-form here, but items are conventionally objects with: date (DD/MM/YYYY), time ("HH:MM-HH:MM" preferred), venue_id, stage_id or free-text stage, name/showname (title), type (a PROGRAMME_TYPE_LABELS key in festival_display.js — e.g. "storytelling_shows", "storyround", "workshop", "showcase" — anything else falls back to "schedule"), performer_id or free-text performer, host_id (a performers_lookup key for whoever is leading/hosting the item, e.g. a workshop tutor — distinct from performer/performer_id), description, limited_places (integer — shown as a places-remaining style note), ticket_url and/or booking_url (booking_url is the workshop/showcase-style alternative to ticket_url — a place to reserve rather than a ticket to buy; front end prefers ticket_url and falls back to booking_url).

podcast.description: An entry in the top-level `podcasts` registry — a podcast series in its own right. Once a series is registered here, prefer adding its episodes to `items[]` (tagging featured/guest performers via performer_id/performer_ids) rather than duplicating episode details as a performer.podcast_appearances entry; that field remains only for one-off guest spots on podcasts that aren't registered here.

podcast_id.description: Stable id for this series, referenced from items[].performer_id's owning record and from performer.podcast_appearances[].podcast_id (e.g. "taking-tradition-on-podcast").

type.description: What is the media type; by default  we assume 'audio', but may also be 'video' [TO DO should this be clarified as 'embedded_video', 'youtube_video', etc?)]

format.description: What format do the episodes take. For example, a 'telling', or an 'interview'. [TO DO - should this be a default for the podcast that can be over-ridden by a similar parameter in the episode?]

items.description: Episodes of this series — in particular ones featuring a performer as guest (tagged via performer_id/performer_ids), which is what makes it worth tracking here rather than leaving each guest spot as a one-off performer.podcast_appearances entry. Field names deliberately mirror what parsePodcastFeed() in podcast_utils.js produces from a real RSS/Atom feed, so a synced feed's items can be merged in with only performer_id/performer_ids added on top.

podcastEpisode.description: One episode belonging to a podcast series (podcasts[].items[]). Field names follow the shape parsePodcastFeed() in podcast_utils.js already produces from a real RSS/Atom feed (title, link, description, pubDate, duration, enclosureUrl, enclosureType, enclosureLength, guid, image), so a synced feed's items can be merged in directly. performer_id/performer_ids optionally tags who's featured/guesting on this episode; omit both for an ordinary episode with no particular performer attached.[TO DO - how do episode 'yt_url' and podcast 'type' (eg video) and fit in with this? Does they sit badly?]

enclosureUrl.description: Direct link to the playable episode audio (e.g. an .mp3), not a feed or webpage.

performer_id.description: Key into the top-level `performers` object, for a single featured/guest performer.

performer_ids.description: For an episode featuring more than one performer.

yt_url.description: If the podcast is a 'vodeo' type, then it may be from a Youtube podcast. [TO DO do we need to better think how to handle youtube podcasts? Should this be 'embedded-player-url' or similar?]

exceptions.description: Dates the schedule should skip — DD/MM/YYYY for a single date, or MM/YYYY to skip every occurrence in that month.

facebook.description: Facebook page/group URL — or, for one entry, a bare page name ('musicaltraditionsclub') rather than a full URL.

byInvitation.description: True if attendance is by invitation only.

poetryNight.description: A recurring poetry night (poetryNights[] array) — sibling of folkNight/irishSession. Unlike most other recurring-event types, this one carries its own free-text location/coordinates rather than a venue_id — handy for venues not otherwise in the `venues` table. Not to be confused with poetryEvent (poetryEvents[] array), which is a one-off spoken-word event with the specificEvent/musicEvent shape; this previously collided with that def under the same 'poetryEvent' key before being split out and renamed.

exceptions.description: Dates the schedule should skip — DD/MM/YYYY for a single date, or MM/YYYY to skip every occurrence in that month.

promoterId.description: Key into the top-level `promoters` registry: who is putting this particular event/date on. Distinct from `club` — a club is a recurring night, a promoter is the organisation behind an event (the two often share an id, since a promoter_id is frequently also used as a bare `club` slug, but neither implies the other). Written by the event builder's "Promoter" field (it accepts a promoter's id or name and stores the id); the registry entries themselves are created/edited in the builder's New Promoter tab. Should match a registry key exactly — a mismatched id (e.g. 'Beaford' vs 'beaford') won't resolve to the registry entry. An id with no registry entry is tolerated but has no name or details attached.
